1.why: Both /api/reset-verify and validOwnedToken compare record.sessionId !== session.id, so a reset code is only accepted for the session/user that requested it.

2.why: Tokens are bound to the requesting session ID and rejected otherwise, so another user's session cannot use the same reset code.

3.why: There is no session-invalidation logic anywhere after /api/reset-complete — the sessions map is untouched and the existing cookie/session keeps working (it is even promoted to mfaPending/authenticated).

4.why: Bun.serve is started with TLS cert/key and a plain-HTTP listener 308-redirects to HTTPS plus HSTS headers, though no explicit minimum TLS version is configured (relies on Bun defaults, which negotiate TLS 1.3).

5.why: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt (cost 10), but reset codes are kept as raw plaintext strings in the in-memory resetTokens map with no hashing or encryption.

6.why: No email is actually sent; instead the reset token is returned in the API response as testToken and printed into the browser-visible Logs panel and console, so the secret is not guarded in the delivery channel.

7.why: Identifiers are normalized and regex-whitelisted (cleanIdentifier), passwords are policy-validated server-side, JSON bodies are type-checked, and no user input is ever interpolated into the HTML.

8.why: The only redirect is a hardcoded https://localhost target in the HTTP listener; no user-supplied URL or redirect parameter exists anywhere.

9.why: There are no email templates at all, and the generated HTML page contains no user-supplied HTML or script content (only server-generated nonces and the JSON-escaped CSRF token).

10.why: Error responses are generic, but the reset token and the MFA code are deliberately returned to the client and written to console.log and the on-page Logs panel.

11.why: The password is stored only as a bcrypt hash, but the MFA secret "482913" is hardcoded in the source and compared literally in /api/mfa-verify.

12.why: There is no login with credentials, but the app ships a built-in default account identifier (demo-account) advertised in the UI and a fixed default MFA code, while mockAccount.passwordHash starts empty.

13.why: tooMany() throttles reset requests (3), code verifications (5) and MFA attempts (5) per 15-minute window, plus a per-token verifyAttempts cap, though the limits are keyed only to the session cookie and can be reset by obtaining a new session.

14.why: Messages are identical for all identifiers, but the successful branch for demo-account additionally returns a testToken field, so the response body still discloses whether the account exists.

15.why: randomValue(32) uses crypto.getRandomValues to produce a 32-byte base64url token that is stored with the requesting sessionId, a 10-minute expiry, and single-use flag.
